notes.text: Patrick Kane is out (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward. Tyler Bertuzzi has taken his spot beside Connor Bedard and Roman Kantserov.

Bowen Byram is on injured reserve and has missed the last 10 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Wyatt Kaiser has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov. That pair has had 32% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 109:51 together, down from 47% with Byram.
Dillon Boucher was added to the roster on Nov 4 and has played beside Cole Smith and Ryan Greene.
Jordan Staal is out 1-2 months (calf tear) and has missed the last 12 games. Mark Jankowski has taken his spot beside Jordan Martinook and Nikolaj Ehlers.
Taylor Hall is out, reported after he played in their last game.

Alexander Nikishin is day to day (not injury related) and has missed the last 10 games. Juuso Välimäki has taken his spot beside Shayne Gostisbehere. That pair has had 70% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 93:50 together.

CAR.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Blackhawks’ best way in is getting good looks.

story.head: The Blackhawks need a win
paras: The Hurricanes won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-2 in Chicago on Oct 10. The Hurricanes (13-3-2) beat the Islanders 5-3 on Thursday, while the Blackhawks are winless in five (0-4-1). Going in, the Hawks are last in the Central (31st in the NHL) and the Hurricanes are first in the NHL.

The Blackhawks haven’t played well, but their record (.265) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .379, and their finishing has held them back. The Hurricanes’ record (.778) is about what their chances are worth.
In their five-game skid, the Blackhawks have been outscored 23-11, including 14-8 at 5-on-5.

The Blackhawks do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest) and don't block many shots (32nd). They also have struggled on the power play (32nd), so their struggling power play gets a tough test from the Hurricanes’ penalty killers. Chicago has scored 2.18 goals a game, the second fewest in the league, and allowed 3.94, the second most. As for the Hurricanes, they take away shots from the point (lowest) and create more chances on the penalty kill than anyone (1st), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd). Carolina has scored 3.83 goals a game, the third most in the league, and allowed 2.33, the third fewest. The Hurricanes are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Blackhawks.

Connor Bedard (4 G / 8 A / 12 P in 11 GP) leads the Blackhawks in scoring, and Roman Kantserov (8 G / 2 A / 10 P in 17 GP) has a team-high eight goals. Sebastian Aho (9 G / 14 A / 23 P in 18 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for ninth in the NHL, and Logan Stankoven (11 G / 6 A / 17 P in 18 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for sixth in the NHL.
Spencer Knight (4-9-0 / .891 SV% in 13 GS) is in line to start for Chicago. Pyotr Kochetkov (10-1-0 / .921 SV% in 11 GS) has been terrific for Carolina and will likely start.

At home, Rod Brind'Amour likes to send Martinook, Jankowski and Jarvis out against opponents’ second lines, so watch for them against Moore, Nazar and Donato. Elsewhere, the Hurricanes usually control more of the chances than the Blackhawks do.
